sections.title: Diaphragm types
sections.live: NO LIVE SECTION → card grid, four cards, from the /products/pads-stoppers-caps component

fields.label: H2
fields.note: 5 words · the heading states the selection criterion instead of labelling the section “Our Range”. Stroke is what decides the shape, and saying so in the heading answers the question before the cards do

fields.label: Intro
paragraphs: The shape follows the stroke. A short stroke can run on a flat diaphragm; a long one needs the sidewall to roll or the convolution to unfold, or the rubber works in tension and tears at the clamp.
marked: The shape follows the stroke. A short stroke can run on a flat diaphragm; a long one needs the sidewall to roll or the convolution to unfold, or the rubber works in tension and tears at the clamp.
fields.note: 38 words · the failure mode is named in the intro because it is the mistake buyers actually make — specifying a flat diaphragm for a stroke that needs a rolling one

fields.label: Cards ×4
rows: A clamped disc, plain or with a moulded-in plate. Simplest to tool and the lowest cost per piece. Stroke is limited to roughly a tenth of the effective diameter before the rubber starts working in tension.
Regulators, pressure switches, low-stroke valve actuators

The sidewall rolls between the piston and the bore instead of stretching, so the effective area stays near constant through the stroke and the force curve is flat. Needs a controlled piston-to-bore gap, which we confirm against your housing drawing.
Metering and dosing pumps, long-stroke actuators, air cylinders

One or more moulded convolutions unfold to give stroke without stretching the rubber. Takes more stroke than a flat diaphragm at the same diameter and tolerates a less precise housing than a rolling one.
Diaphragm pumps, sprayer heads, large actuators

Nylon, polyester or aramid fabric bonded into the moulding. The fabric carries the pressure load and holds the effective area stable; the elastomer seals and takes the chemical duty. Any of the three shapes above can be reinforced.
Anything above roughly 3 bar, and any duty where stretch would change the dose
fields.note:
Four cards, and the fourth is a construction rather than a shape — that is deliberate and the card says so in its last sentence. Reinforcement is the question a pressure application turns on, and burying it inside the other three would hide the capability that wins the enquiry. Section 05 covers it properly.
No card carries a pressure rating. A rating belongs to a part — its diameter, its ply count, its clamp — not to a shape. Publishing a generic one is the same class of claim as the bellows cycle counts

notes: Card titles are <h3> under the section <h2>. Four real subheadings, and each is a term buyers search: rolling diaphragm, convoluted diaphragm and fabric-reinforced diaphragm are all distinct queries.
All four cards in the DOM at first paint. If this grid is built as a filter or a carousel, every card is hidden with CSS, never conditionally rendered.
Internal links on the application names, not on “read more”: metering and dosing pumps → /industries/pumps-valves, sprayer heads → /industries/agriculture.

We bond nylon, polyester or aramid fabric into the moulding: the fabric takes the pressure load and holds the effective area constant through the stroke, and the elastomer seals and carries the chemical duty. Ply count, weave and orientation follow your pressure and stroke — send both and we will specify them.

sections.title: Technical & commercial questions
sections.live: NO LIVE SECTION → FAQ accordion, six questions, from the /products/bellows component · these six are the FAQPage mainEntity, verbatim

fields.label: Q1

lines: What is the minimum order quantity for diaphragms?

parts.text: We supply in bulk. The minimum run is 10,000 pieces per part number, per compound, or quoted against the part where geometry or tooling makes that unrealistic. Prototype and first-article lots sit outside the minimum.

fields.note: 36 words · client-instructed 2026-09-01, the standard answer used across the set. Do not reword it and do not add a second number — the live site states an MOQ about ninety times, including twice in one FAQ answer in two different figures

fields.label: Q2

lines: How long will the diaphragm last?

parts.text: We do not publish a cycle figure, because we do not own a fatigue rig and a number without a test behind it is worthless to you. What we will do is qualify against your duty: give us the stroke, the working pressure and the target cycle life, and we will propose a compound and construction, run samples, and have them tested at a named laboratory to ISO 132, ASTM D430 or ASTM D813 — with the report in your name.

fields.note: 78 words · the most important answer on the page. Cycle life is the first thing a pump engineer asks and the easiest claim to fabricate; the bellows page had four invented cycle ratings removed for exactly this reason. Refusing the number and offering the test is a stronger commercial position than a published figure, because a published figure is read as a warranty and this offer is read as competence. It is also the only honest answer available

fields.label: Q3

lines: Can you reverse-engineer a diaphragm from a failed sample?

parts.text: Yes. Send the old diaphragm and tell us how it failed. We size from the housing and the stroke rather than from the worn part, and the failure tells us what to change — hardened and cracked means heat, swollen and distorted means the wrong compound for the medium, split at the clamp line means the stroke or the housing rather than the rubber.

fields.note: 64 words · the same diagnostic framing as section 03, which is deliberate: a buyer who skips to the FAQ gets the same answer as one who reads the page

fields.label: Q4

parts.text: Yes. Nylon, polyester and aramid are all bonded in-house during cure, with ply count and orientation specified against your pressure and stroke. Metal inserts — steel, stainless or brass — are moulded in the same way, so there is no adhesive joint to fail.

fields.note: 45 words · answers the qualifying question a pressure application turns on, and surfaces the bonding capability that appears nowhere else on the site

fields.label: Q5

lines: Are your diaphragms approved for drinking water or food contact?

parts.text: No, and we will not imply otherwise. Potable-water approval is granted to a specific compound formulation held by the compound supplier, not to a polymer and not to us — the schemes are WRAS to BS 6920 in the UK, NSF/ANSI/CAN 61 in North America, AS/NZS 4020 in Australia and New Zealand, and KTW-BWGL with DVGW W270 in Germany. Tell us which scheme your market requires and we will confirm what we can supply against it. We hold no food-contact or pharmaceutical approvals.

fields.note: 82 words · the exact position from sheets 24 and 28, and the reason it belongs on this page specifically: dosing and metering pumps are a water-treatment product, so this is the page where a buyer will assume approval unless told. Answering “no” first and then being useful is what makes the rest of the page credible

fields.label: Q6

lines: What are your payment and delivery terms for international orders?

parts.text: TT and LC accepted, discussed per order. Ex-works Nashik or FOB Nhava Sheva. Commercial invoice, packing list and certificate of origin are issued with every consignment. Production is three to four weeks from drawing approval, or two weeks on an express basis where we have confirmed capacity.

fields.note: 48 words · the standard commercial string, unchanged. The lead time matches every other page — 3–4 weeks standard, 2 weeks express. Not 14–21 days, which is the live site’s figure and promises faster than the company delivers
